about.title: Orland Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Orland residents rely on all kinds of everyday products, from farm equipment used around Glenn County's agricultural land to household appliances and vehicle parts driven along Walker Street and Rt 32. When one of these products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can upend a family's routine fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning the focus stays on whether the product itself was defective rather than trying to prove a manufacturer was careless. That distinction matters in a smaller community like Orland, where the injured person is rarely the one with an inside view into how a product was built or tested. We handle product liability claims directly and can review what happened and explain your options. If a product hurt you or someone in your household, preserving that item and documenting the incident are good first steps while you decide what to do next.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us About a Defective Product Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Proof
items.desc: California generally lets injured people focus on showing the product was defective and caused harm, rather than digging into a manufacturer's internal decisions or negligence.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which we can help sort out based on how the product moved through the supply chain.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because the defect itself is central to a strict liability claim, keeping the product intact and unaltered can make a real difference in how the case is evaluated.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally need to show the product had a defect and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer failed to use reasonable care. We can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including any packaging, instructions, or parts involved. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Is this kind of claim common in a smaller area like Orland?
items.answer: Defective product injuries can happen anywhere, whether it's equipment used on a Glenn County farm or a household item picked up at a local store. We can handle product liability claims for Orland residents regardless of the city's size.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No, our initial consultation is free. We typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
